It rests on one high draw and has had no off-seed check. H2.10.4 now doubles as that check.\n- **Head-lr line closed.** H7.3 is supported (tuned at 0.5x). H7.3.4 is refuted, recorded as \"no gain; flat between 0.4x and 0.5x\" rather than a proven optimum. H7.3.3 (head wd) is inconclusive, H7.3.1 retired.\n- **MaxSup (H6.6).** Refuted, but only at α=0.3. Phase-dependent label smoothing (H6.7) has a lower prior: the search shows its cited support did not cover label smoothing, and another paper (TSLA) points the opposite way.\n- **Hand-fused BN backward (H2.16, H2.16.3).** H2.16 is refuted and H2.16.3 retired. BN backward needs per-channel reductions over the whole activation before it can write the input gradient, so it cannot be done in one pass.\n- **Whitening-bias freeze (H2.15).** Re-sourced to hiverge and airbench, which actually skip the compute, unlike Fable. The expected saving rises to ≥1%, and the freeze point is aligned with E061's tested 20%.\n- **Width cuts (H2.13).** Re-framed around tile quantization: 352 and 320 both round up on 128-wide tiles, so 256 is the clean test point.\n- **Per-phase batch size.** H2.11.1 now carries E043- as its evidence. H2.11 is reopened for the mirror split.\n- **Margin check (H4.2.5).** Supported at its boundary (off-seed 0.7530).\n- **H4.** The pooling rule now uses code diffs, not description labels, plus a ±0.6% band for time deltas.\n\n**New hypotheses**\n- **N_pin:** a pinned staging buffer for the trial-1 slow-transfer window.\n- **N_bs:** bs 1536 at low resolution with bs 1024 in the 32 px phase.\n- **N9 (new Lvl1):** accuracy now has to come from structural changes, because scalar knobs are exhausted at the noise floor.\n- **N9a / N9a1:** hiverge and Fable's decaying renorm target norm, which acts as an implicit learning-rate schedule.\n\n**Recommended order**\n1. Diff the tip against the tail commit.\n2. Add the tail to E070, with an off-seed check on seeds 3-10.\n3. The real whitening-bias freeze.\n4. Trim the 32 px phase by 0.25 epoch.\n5. Muon filter lr 0.28 and the renorm-target decay as off-seed A/Bs.\n6. The batch split."}

updates.statement: Per-epoch GPU work drives the score. Current tip: E070/E071 (2@16 + 1.25@24 + 4@32, 7.25 ep), pooled 0.7537 at ~4.58 s. Its off-seed mean on seeds 3-10 is 0.7530 (E077). Its provenance is unresolved: the stated base a1aef09 predates the tail commit 766d5bf, so it probably lacks the Fable tail. Cost structure: the 32 px tail is ~71% of time and energy-bound; 16 px is low-occupancy but 98% GPU-busy. Remaining time levers, ranked: (a) a real whitening-bias freeze via detach or requires_grad (H2.15; search estimate 1-2.5%); (b) a fractional trim of the 32 px phase, untested on any Muon base (H2.10.5); (c) a pinned staging buffer for the trial-1 slow-H2D window (~0.6% of the local 3-trial mean only; H2.14.4); (d) width cuts, only at tile-aligned widths and only after a per-layer profile (H2.13). Closed: CUDA graphs and launch levers (E052), Inductor pointwise tuning (E066), hand-fused BN backward (no one-pass form exists without cuDNN conv-epilogue stats, which torch 2.4 does not expose), cuDNN determinism in scored runs (E036), prepare (banked in E060).
updates.reason: Restated with the E071-E078 results, the unresolved tail provenance, the search findings (BN backward has no one-pass form; hiverge detach freeze; tile quantization) and the review's untested 32 px trim. The lever ranking was reordered.

updates.statement: Step-indexed schedule reshuffles and trims are the finest schedule lever. Under the rule-consistent pooling (head-lr family ~0.7550 incl. E066), the 7.0-8.0-epoch low-res variants form a noise plateau: E064/E065 2@16+1.5@24 = 0.7552; E070/E071 2@16+1.25@24 = 0.7537; E072/E073 1.5@16+1.5@24 = 0.7532; the 3@16+1@24 head-lr family = 0.7550. All are within ~1 SE, so no reshuffle has a measured effect. If E070 lacks the tail, its like-for-like cost against the parent E064/E065 is -0.15 pp for -2.7% (~0.055 pp per 1%), not 0.14 pp per 1%. Fractional trims of the 32 px phase (~71% of time) have never been tested on a Muon base. The claim that the 32 px tail is binding rests only on E025 (an older base with whole-epoch moves).
updates.reason: The review showed the deltas were taken against inconsistent baselines (the tail pool for E070, a non-rule family for E064). Rewritten as a plateau. Confidence lowered.

The prereg's absolute bar (pooled >=0.7540) was met (0.7552), but against the rule-consistent head-lr family (~0.7550) the reshuffle is +0.02 pp for +0.9% time, which is inside time noise. So there is no evidence that 2@16+1.5@24 beats 3@16+1@24. E070/E071 (0.7537) do not separate either.

updates.statement: The E070 code (e945ed5) lacks the Fable tail, which a free git diff against a1aef09 and 766d5bf will show. If so, add the tail unchanged to 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 4@32. Prediction: a two-run pooled accuracy >=0.7555 and an off-seed seeds 3-10 mean >= the no-tail E070 off-seed mean (0.7530) + 0.1 pp, at time within ±0.6% of 4.583 s. The same off-seed A/B is the tail's first off-seed check (H6.5.2). If the diff shows the tail is already present, the tail and the 24 px trim do not stack, and the tail pool (0.7562) was a high draw.
updates.reason: Still the top-priority experiment per the review. The off-seed arm was added so the run doubles as the missing tail check, and the time band was widened to the measured ±0.6% noise.

updates.statement: On the verified tip (after H2.10.4), cut the 32 px phase by 0.25 epoch (... + 3.75@32, step-indexed switch, LR/EMA/lookahead/renorm/tail rescaled to the step count). Prediction: time drops ~4-5% (~0.2 s), and accuracy falls by <=0.2 pp (two scored runs plus an off-seed seeds 3-10 check), i.e. <=0.05 pp per 1%. That is at least as good as the ~0.055 pp per 1% measured for the 24 px trim against its correct parent. If the loss is >=0.3 pp, the 32 px phase is binding and trims must come from elsewhere.
updates.reason: Threshold re-anchored to the corrected 24 px trim rate (~0.055 pp per 1%). The review ranks this as the largest untested engineering-free time lever.

updates.statement: Per-phase batch size. Per-step costs dominate the cheap 16/24 px phases (E038: ~2 ms per removed step there), while the 32 px tail is energy-bound. The tested direction, a larger batch in the low-res phases (E043, bs 2048 at 16/24 px), cost 0.49 pp: large early batches hurt. The untested mirror keeps bs 1536 at 16/24 px, where the step savings are, and returns the 32 px tail to bs 1024. If bs 1536's accuracy cost (~0.13-0.3 pp, E038) arose mainly in the tail, this recovers it for a modest per-step cost at 32 px.
updates.reason: Reopened per the review. The E043 direction is refuted, but the mirror split is untested and is a structural accuracy source (see the new structural Lvl1).

Evidence token added. E043 ran exactly this design (bs 2048 at 16/24 px, bs 1024 at 32 px, sample-indexed schedules). Time 5.159 s met the bar, but accuracy was 0.7493 against the >=0.755 prediction (-0.49 pp). Evidence: E043-.

updates.statement: Muon flattened the epoch slope, so a group-2 width cut might trade like a schedule trim. E050 (384->352) saved only half its FLOP-proportional time. NVIDIA's tile-quantization guidance explains this: 352 rounds up to 3x128-wide N-tiles, the same work as 384, and 320 does too on 128-wide tiles. Only tile-aligned widths (256, or 320 if cuDNN picks 64-wide tiles) can save FLOP-proportional time. A cut to 256 is a large capacity loss (E017: 320 cost 0.94 pp under SGD), so the prior for a profitable width cut stays low. Decide with existing profile data and a per-layer profile, never with a scored run first.
updates.reason: The search's tile-quantization finding gives a mechanism for E050 and implies 320 is not a clean test point either. The prior stays low because of the capacity cost.

updates.statement: First analyze the group-2 per-layer times that E067 was asked to log. If they are missing, run an untimed per-layer CUDA-event profile at 32 px, bs 1536, on the tip with group-2 widths 384, 352, 320 and 256, and record the chosen cuDNN kernel tile shapes. Prediction: 352 and 320 each recover <=60% of their FLOP-proportional group-2 time, while 256 recovers >=80%, i.e. tile quantization on 128-wide tiles. If 256 also recovers <80%, width cuts are dead and H2.13 is refuted.
updates.reason: Updated with the search's tile-quantization argument (320 is likely also misaligned on 128-wide tiles) and the review's note that E067's profile data may already exist.

Unchanged verdict (E076: the penalty is a post-build slow pageable-H2D window, not lazy init). Per the review, the pinned-memory fix is now tracked separately as H2.14.4, because ~0.08 s on trial 1 is ~0.6% of the local 3-trial mean.

updates.statement: A real whitening-bias freeze is a FLOP/byte time lever. Detach the bias in forward (hiverge: b.detach() keyed on a bool) or set requires_grad=False (airbench: 'disable their gradient to increase backward-pass throughput ... without reducing accuracy'). The stem output then needs no grad, so autograd skips group-1 conv1's dgrad (~1.9% of conv FLOPs per step, with 24 output channels and poor tensor-core efficiency), the stem GELU backward and the bias reduction over 1536x24x31x31. The search estimate is ~1-2.5% of time, and as a FLOP lever it should transfer to the 300 W PCIe judge. Fable e1 only zeroes the LR, which is equivalent to E061 and saves nothing. E061 froze via LR=0 at 20% of steps at -0.08 pp (within noise), which covers the accuracy side only for a freeze at 20% of steps, not at ~0.2 epoch.
updates.reason: Attribution corrected per the search (hiverge/airbench do the compute-saving freeze, Fable does not). Expected saving raised. Accuracy-precondition scope narrowed per the review.

updates.statement: On the verified tip, detach the whitening bias (hiverge pattern) from step 0.2*total onward, i.e. E061's freeze point, which falls inside the 16 px phase. Use two static compiled graphs keyed on whiten_bias_grad; only the 16 px shape needs both variants, and all are warmed up in build on synthetic data. Confirm in the compiled backward graph that group-1 conv1's dgrad and the stem backward are gone. Prediction: two scored runs average >=1.0% below the base's pooled time (outside the ±0.6% noise band), with accuracy within 0.1 pp of the base on the off-seed seeds 3-10 check. If the time drop is <0.4%, the dgrad is not skipped or is negligible, and H2.15 is refuted as a time lever. Move to an earlier freeze (~0.2 epoch) only after the saving is verified.
updates.reason: Freeze point aligned with E061's tested point (review). Threshold raised to >=1% from the search FLOP estimate. Two runs required, because the lever is below the time-noise floor for a single run.

Inductor flag tuning is closed (E066). The search shows a one-pass BN backward is impossible: the per-channel reductions span N·H·W (~1.48M elements per channel at 32 px) before dX can be written, and the activation is far larger than on-chip memory. The 2-pass structure profiled in E067 is already the floor without cuDNN genStats epilogue fusion, which torch 2.4 does not expose. No viable lever remains.

Infeasible as stated: dy and x cannot be read only once, because dX depends on global per-channel reductions (search: PyTorch MixOrderReduction is limited to rows of <=16384 elements and to LN/RMSNorm). Retired without a run.

updates.statement: Accuracy noise sets the usable margin, and near-gate decisions select for luck. The per-run sd of the 3-seed mean is ~0.15 pp, the same size as the zero-cost effects being chased. Pooling rule: - Every same-math run counts, whatever its sign; math-neutral variants count (reduction order, static shapes, pool swap, prepare fusion, Inductor flags). - Bit-identical reruns count once (E044/E045, E062/E067, E071/E076). - Family membership is decided by code diffs and source hashes, never by base labels in descriptions (E067 was labeled E060 code but was bit-identical to E062). Under this rule the head-lr family is ~0.7550 (E062, E063, E066). Since E077 the off-seed seeds 3-10 A/B is in use: tip 0.7530, 0.4x head 0.7523, MaxSup 0.7512. Time noise between same-code runs is ~0.5-0.8%, so single-run time deltas under ±0.6% are not evidence, and math-neutral levers predicted at <1% need two runs. The official gate is a 40-seed mean.
updates.reason: Added the description-label unreliability and the E071/E076 bit-identical pair (review), the off-seed results now available, and the ±0.6% time-delta rule.

updates.statement: Provenance check, untimed, and the next action before any scored run. Diff e945ed5 (E070) against a1aef09 (E064) and 766d5bf (E068) to establish whether the tip contains the Fable tail. Diff 772c536 (E077) and bc2ffe6 (E078) against e945ed5 to establish their actual base, since they were described as 'on the verified tail tip' with no verification. Diff 8146343 (E067) against 026a301 (E060) and 8d69aa4 (E062), since E067 was bit-identical to E062. Earlier checks: e6c8e93/4fd9ea5 vs 2fda094, and 5a77f89/6262ecd. Any failure removes the affected runs from the pooled baselines, and the deltas from E070 onward must then be recomputed.
updates.reason: Extended to E077/E078/E067 per the review, which found that the base labels cannot be trusted.

E077 measured the tip (E070 code, presumably) off-seed on seeds 3-10: 0.7530. That is >=0.7530 and within 0.07 pp of the seeds 0-2 pool (0.7537), so the prediction holds, but only at its boundary. The local margin is ~0; the official 75% gate has ~0.3 pp. The verdict depends on H4.2.4 confirming which code E077's tip arm ran. Evidence: E077+.

updates.statement: Untimed analysis of logs that already exist: per-seed final-weight checksums for E062 and E067 (bit-identical per-seed accuracy) and for E071 and E076 (bit-identical), plus any diverging same-code pair (E068/E069, E064/E065). Prediction: the bit-identical-accuracy pairs have identical weight checksums, and every seed whose accuracy differs between reruns has a different checksum (train divergence). No seed has identical weights but different accuracy; if one does, eval-shape cuDNN picks are a separate source and should be pinned in build. Run new diagnostics only if the logs are missing.
updates.reason: Per the review, the bit-identical pairs E062/E067 and E071/E076 already exist and checksums were logged, so analyze before spending runs.
No change in evidence. The kernel-name logs requested in E067 have not been analyzed (review); analyze them before any new instrumentation.

updates.statement: Zero-time-cost scalar accuracy levers have to fund schedule cuts, and their measured effects are about the size of decision noise. Since E057: - Muon floor 0.05: null (E057/E058). - Warmup length: closed both directions (E051, E059). - Whitening-bias LR freeze: null (E061). - Head Muon lr 0.5x: ~+0.15-0.2 pp against the pre-head-lr family (supported). - 0.4x: not better, flat within ~0.1 pp off-seed (E077). - Head wd: null (E074/E075). - MaxSup α=0.3: worse (-0.18 pp off-seed, E078). - Fable tail: +~0.12 pp, never checked off-seed. Of ~10 scalar levers tried at 1.5-2 SE thresholds, only head lr survived. Remaining scalar candidates are low prior: phase-dependent LS (H6.7) and Muon filter lr transfer (H7.1.3). The structural alternatives are tracked under the new structural Lvl1. Decide everything with an off-seed seeds 3-10 A/B plus scored runs.
updates.reason: Added E074/E075/E077/E078 outcomes. The pattern (scalar knobs null, structural changes positive) motivates the new Lvl1 suggested by the review.

updates.statement: The SGD-era end-of-run schedule did not suit Muon in the ~256-step regime. A floor change alone did nothing (E057/E058). Fable's tail (decay ends ~4% early and holds at the 0.05 floor, lookahead stops, light final EMA over the last ~8 steps, eval on EMA weights with BN buffers from the net) pooled 0.7562 (E068/E069), about +0.12 pp over the rule-consistent baseline, mostly from one high draw, with no off-seed check. Fable designed the tail to remove '±0.1-0.2% plateau wobble', i.e. to cut end-of-run variance, so its main benefit may be a lower per-seed sd rather than a higher mean, which still helps a 40-seed gate. If the EMA component carries the gain, the next axis is the averaging design (e.g. LAWA-style uniform average of the last k snapshots), without BN re-estimation (E018).
updates.reason: Integrated the search findings (Fable's variance-reduction intent, LAWA) and the review's note that the tail has not been checked off-seed.

The prereg (pooled >=0.7548) was met (0.7562), but the result rests mostly on E068's high draw (E069 0.7544), is ~+0.12 pp against the rule-consistent baseline 0.7550 (~1 SE), and has never been checked off-seed. Confidence lowered; H2.10.4's off-seed A/B serves as the confirmation.

updates.statement: Gated on H2.10.4 showing an off-seed tail gain >=0.1 pp. On the verified tail tip, run two single-change ablations: (a) remove only the final EMA (eval on the net weights, floor-hold and lookahead stop kept) and (b) remove only the floor-hold (decay ends at the last step, final EMA kept). Each gets one scored run plus an off-seed seeds 3-10 check, and each reports the mean and the per-seed sd. Prediction: one component accounts for >=2/3 of the tail's mean gain, so ablating it costs >=0.1 pp off-seed, while ablating the other costs <=0.05 pp. If neither moves the mean but (a) raises the per-seed sd by >=30%, the EMA's value is variance reduction.
updates.reason: Gated per the review, with an sd measurement added per the search (Fable's tail targets wobble).

updates.statement: MaxSup (CE + α(z_max − mean_k z_k)) in place of label smoothing 0.3 was tested only at α=0.3, an arbitrary transfer from LS ε, because α scales a logit gap rather than a probability mass. At that setting it was worse on both instruments (scored -0.35 pp, off-seed -0.18 pp, E078): LS's target-side term matters in this regime. Other α values are untested but low prior; this is not a general closure of the loss family (see H6.7).
updates.reason: Scope narrowed to α=0.3 per the review. Both the off-seed and the scored instrument agree on a negative effect.
E078: off-seed 0.7512 vs tip 0.7530 (-0.18 pp), scored 0.7502. The prediction of >= tip +0.15 pp failed on both instruments. The refutation applies to α=0.3 only. Evidence: E078-.

updates.statement: Phase-dependent label smoothing. The original motivation was EfficientNetV2's adaptive regularization (+0.7-0.8 pp), but that covered dropout/RandAugment/mixup, not LS. TSLA (CIFAR-100, 200 epochs) found the opposite direction: drop LS late. Uniform LS changes were null (E009, E037) and MaxSup failed (E078). The prior is low; if run at all, the TSLA-direction arm (lower LS in the final ~20%) is better supported than lower LS early.
updates.reason: The search undercuts the cited support and points in the opposite direction; prior lowered.
Prior lowered per the search (EfficientNetV2's gain did not include LS; TSLA points the other way). Low priority.

updates.statement: Optimizer quality per update was the binding constraint on CIFAR-100 at ~8 epochs, and Muon was the lever. On the 9 group convs it gave +1.14 pp at equal epochs (E019), a flatter epoch slope (E020) and large-batch tolerance (E022, E038). Head on Muon: ~+0.15 pp (indirect pooled estimate). Head lr 0.5x: ~+0.15-0.2 pp against the pre-head-lr family. Head lr 0.4x was not better (E077, flat within ~0.1 pp off-seed), and head wd was null (E074/E075). The head line is closed at 0.5x. Untested on the bs-1536, ~256-step, head-on-Muon base: the filter Muon lr (H7.1.3), which is a zero-cost 0-d tensor knob. Cheaper orthogonalizers are closed (E031, E033, search).
updates.reason: Head-side results E074/E075/E077 integrated; H7.1.3 flagged as the remaining untested Muon knob, per the review.

updates.statement: On the verified tip (bs 1536, ~240 steps, head on Muon at 0.5x), change only the conv-filter Muon lr from 0.24 to 0.28; the head lr stays 0.5x of the filter lr, so it scales along. This is a 0-d tensor change and nothing recompiles. Decide with an off-seed seeds 3-10 A/B against the tip (0.7530) plus two scored runs. Prediction: off-seed mean >= tip +0.12 pp. If it is within ±0.1 pp, run 0.20 off-seed only; if both are flat, the bs-1024 optimum transfers and Muon lr is closed.
updates.reason: Re-anchored to the current tip and the off-seed instrument. The review notes it has been open since ~E046 while lower-prior knobs ran first.

updates.statement: The head's update scale was a live accuracy knob, and it is now tuned. Moving the head to Muon helped (~+0.15 pp), and lowering its lr from 1x to 0.5x helped (head-lr family ~0.7550 vs 0.7531). Going further to 0.4x (near the spectral-condition value sqrt(100/576) ≈ 0.42) was not better: -0.07 pp off-seed, within noise, so the response is flat in 0.4-0.5x. Bounding the head norm with decoupled wd was null (+0.07 pp, E074/E075). The head line is closed at 0.5x.
updates.reason: Rolled up from H7.3.2 (supported), H7.3.3 (null) and H7.3.4 (no gain): the knob was real but is exhausted.
A diagnostic of the mechanism (orthogonalization vs step size) with no time or accuracy payoff, now that head lr is closed at 0.5x.

E062/E063 pooled 0.75395 against the 0.7540 bar (at it within rounding). With E066 (math-neutral) counted, the head-lr family is ~0.7550 vs the 7-run pre-head-lr family at 0.7531 (+0.19 pp, ~2 SE). E049 agrees. Evidence: E062~ E063+.

E074/E075 pooled 0.7544 against the tip pool 0.7537 (+0.07 pp) missed the >=0.7548 bar. The run pair is wide (0.7557/0.7532) and there is no off-seed check, so it is within noise. Not pursued: the prior was low and the head line is closed. Evidence: E074~ E075~.

The prediction (0.4x >= 0.5x +0.05 pp) failed on both instruments: off-seed -0.07 pp, scored -0.31 pp (single run). The pre-registered 'clearly worse' bar (>=0.1 pp worse) was met only by the single scored run, not off-seed. The correct reading is 'no gain; head lr flat in 0.4-0.5x within ~0.1 pp', not an established optimum at 0.5x. The base must be confirmed by H4.2.4.

new.statement: The trial-1 penalty (prepare 0.098 s vs 0.019 s in trials 2-3, E076) is a slow pageable host-to-device window after build. In build, allocate an empty pinned host staging buffer and a GPU destination of the dataset's shape (no real data). In prepare, copy the uint8 training array into the pinned buffer and upload with non_blocking=True, followed by one sync. This is math-neutral. Prediction: trial-1 prepare <=0.04 s, trials 2-3 prepare not slower than 0.025 s, and per-seed accuracy bit-identical or within noise. The mean time falls by ~0.4-0.6%; per-trial prepare logs decide, because a single run's total is inside time noise. If trial-1 prepare stays >=0.08 s, the window is not specific to pageable memory and the line is closed.

On the verified tip, keep bs 1536 for the 16/24 px phases and use bs 1024 for the 32 px phase. LR warmup/decay, the tail, EMA, lookahead and renorm are indexed by samples seen; the SGD groups are scaled per phase by the kilostep rule; Muon lr/momentum are unchanged. The bs-1024 32 px shape is static and warmed up in build. Pre-registered time cost: about +64 steps at 32 px under the power cap, i.e. +1.5-3% (4.65-4.72 s). Prediction: an off-seed seeds 3-10 mean >= tip +0.15 pp and a two-run scored pool >= tip pool +0.1 pp, i.e. accuracy bought at >=0.055 pp per 1% of time, so it beats the corrected trim rate and can fund a 32 px trim. If the gain is <=0.05 pp, bs 1536's accuracy cost did not arise in the tail, and H2.11 is closed.

At ~7-8 epochs and ~240 steps, the remaining accuracy deficit is set by structural properties of training, not by scalar hyperparameters. Structural properties here means how update count and quality are allocated across resolution phases, the effective step-size schedule that Muon plus filter renorm imply, and the end-of-run averaging design. Every structural change so far bought >=0.15 pp: Muon +1.14 (E019), head on Muon ~+0.15, the 24 px bridge (E032: -0.68 without it), and possibly the tail. Every scalar knob since E057 was null within ±0.1 pp or negative: floor, warmup in both directions, bias LR freeze, head lr 0.4x, head wd, MaxSup, LS 0.2, Muon momentum and lr on older bases. Implication: rank new accuracy candidates by expected structural effect (>=0.15 pp) and stop generating scalar-knob variants.

The Muon filters feed BN, so the effective relative update size is (Muon step)/||w||, and the renorm target norm acts as a second, implicit LR schedule. hiverge and Fable decay the renorm target linearly from 0.5012 to 0.0786 over the run. Combined with the LR decay to 0.05x, that keeps the relative step from collapsing late (it ends at ~0.3x instead of 0.05x of its start value). The tip adopted hiverge's renorm cadence (E035), but the tree has never examined its target-norm schedule. If the tip renorms to a constant norm, its late relative step is much smaller than in the CIFAR-10 SOTA recipes. This is a change of schedule shape across the whole run, not the end-only floor change that E057 found null.

First check in the tip code whether filter renorm uses a constant target (free, no run). If it does, change only the target to decay linearly from the tip's current value c to 0.157c over training (hiverge's 0.5012->0.0786 ratio), computed from progress inside the compiled update as a 0-d tensor so nothing recompiles. Change nothing else. Prediction: an off-seed seeds 3-10 mean >= tip +0.15 pp and a two-run scored pool >= tip pool +0.1 pp, at time within ±0.6%. If the off-seed delta is within ±0.1 pp, the implicit schedule is not binding and N9a is refuted. If the tip already decays its target, retire N9a without a run.

structured_output.summary:
The first step is free: diff the tip's code against the tail commit (H4.2.4). The tip (E070/E071, 4.58 s, pooled 0.7537) probably lacks the Fable tail. Until that diff is done, the bases of E077 and E078 are also unverified.

**Tree changes**
- **Re-pooling.** I recomputed the deltas against the rule-consistent head-lr family (~0.7550). The 7.0-7.5-epoch low-res reshuffles then form a noise plateau. H2.10.3 moves to inconclusive. If the tip lacks the tail, the 24 px trim costs ~0.055 pp per 1% of time against its correct parent, not 0.14.
- **Tail (H6.5.2).** Still supported, but confidence is lowered to 0.35. It rests on one high draw and has had no off-seed check. H2.10.4 now doubles as that check.
- **Head-lr line closed.** H7.3 is supported (tuned at 0.5x). H7.3.4 is refuted, recorded as "no gain; flat between 0.4x and 0.5x" rather than a proven optimum. H7.3.3 (head wd) is inconclusive, H7.3.1 retired.
- **MaxSup (H6.6).** Refuted, but only at α=0.3. Phase-dependent label smoothing (H6.7) has a lower prior: the search shows its cited support did not cover label smoothing, and another paper (TSLA) points the opposite way.
- **Hand-fused BN backward (H2.16, H2.16.3).** H2.16 is refuted and H2.16.3 retired. BN backward needs per-channel reductions over the whole activation before it can write the input gradient, so it cannot be done in one pass.
- **Whitening-bias freeze (H2.15).** Re-sourced to hiverge and airbench, which actually skip the compute, unlike Fable. The expected saving rises to ≥1%, and the freeze point is aligned with E061's tested 20%.
- **Width cuts (H2.13).** Re-framed around tile quantization: 352 and 320 both round up on 128-wide tiles, so 256 is the clean test point.
- **Per-phase batch size.** H2.11.1 now carries E043- as its evidence. H2.11 is reopened for the mirror split.
- **Margin check (H4.2.5).** Supported at its boundary (off-seed 0.7530).
- **H4.** The pooling rule now uses code diffs, not description labels, plus a ±0.6% band for time deltas.

**New hypotheses**
- **N_pin:** a pinned staging buffer for the trial-1 slow-transfer window.
- **N_bs:** bs 1536 at low resolution with bs 1024 in the 32 px phase.
- **N9 (new Lvl1):** accuracy now has to come from structural changes, because scalar knobs are exhausted at the noise floor.
- **N9a / N9a1:** hiverge and Fable's decaying renorm target norm, which acts as an implicit learning-rate schedule.

**Recommended order**
1. Diff the tip against the tail commit.
2. Add the tail to E070, with an off-seed check on seeds 3-10.
3. The real whitening-bias freeze.
4. Trim the 32 px phase by 0.25 epoch.
5. Muon filter lr 0.28 and the renorm-target decay as off-seed A/Bs.
6. The batch split.
